walkthroughs.body_html:
The Roman Catholic Church teaches Purgatory — a state of purification for those who die in God's grace but still need cleansing (Catechism 1030).

Catholics pray for the dead. Most Protestants reject Purgatory — heaven is by grace through faith alone.

Muslims teach Barzakh — a waiting state between death and Resurrection.

Near-death experiences (NDEs) — bright light, tunnel, life review — are sometimes cited as evidence. Critics say these can be explained by brain chemistry under stress.

Mediums claim to contact the dead. Most Christian churches reject this (Deuteronomy 18:11 forbids it). Islam strictly forbids fortune-telling and contacting the dead.

Christian funerals usually include scripture, prayers, hymns, a sermon and committal — burial or cremation. Catholic funerals include a Requiem Mass.

Islamic Janazah: the body is washed, shrouded in white cloth, prayed over and buried — facing Mecca — as soon as possible (ideally within 24 hours). Cremation is not allowed.
